questionnaire.name: SmartUrbanity - Your Experience With Cycling and E-scooters

welcome_page.title: Welcome to Your Experience With Cycling and E-scooters
welcome_page.image_alt: #Bicycle and a route between two points
welcome_page.description:
This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience riding a bicycle, e-bike or e-scooter. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when riding a bicycle or e-scooter in the city, and identify opportunities to make these trips safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

final_page.title: Thank you!
final_page.description: Your submission has been recorded. Thank you for taking the time to complete the questionnaire.

questionnaire.title: 8. Your Experience With Cycling and E-scooters

sections.title: Bicycle or e-scooter use and traffic
sections.description: Questions about whether you ride a bicycle or e-scooter and how you feel in traffic.

questions.text: Do you ride a bicycle (including e-bikes) or an e-scooter, your own or a shared one, at least once a week to get to places?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.text: What keeps you from riding a bicycle or e-scooter, or from riding more often? (Select all that apply)
questions.help: We ask this to understand what limits cycling and e-scooter use for different people. Answering is optional, and you can also choose not to say.

options.text: I don't need to: other ways of getting around suit me better
Hills and steep slopes
Traffic feels too dangerous
No cycle lanes or no continuous routes to where I go
Nowhere secure to keep it at home or to park it at my destination
I don't have a bicycle or e-scooter, and there is no sharing service near me
It costs too much (the vehicle or the sharing service)
I don't know how to ride a bicycle or e-scooter, or I don't feel up to it
My health, a disability or my age makes it difficult
Destinations are too far away
Heat or bad weather
I carry heavy things or accompany children or other people

questions.text: Which type of bicycle or e-scooter do you use most often?
questions.help: A cargo bike has a large box or platform for carrying children or goods. Shared bikes with a station are picked up and returned at fixed points; those without a station can be left anywhere within the service area.

options.text: Standard pedal bicycle (private)
Electric bicycle / e-bike (private)
Shared / hire bicycle (docked or dockless)
Shared / hire e-bike
Cargo bike or adapted bike
E-scooter (private)
Shared / hire e-scooter

questions.text: How comfortable do you feel riding your bicycle or e-scooter in urban traffic in your city?

options.text: Very comfortable — I ride in all conditions without difficulty
Fairly comfortable — I manage most situations
Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable
Not very comfortable — I ride in traffic only when I have no alternative
Not at all comfortable
I don't ride in urban traffic

questions.text: How confident are you in your ability to anticipate and react to dangerous situations while riding (e.g., car doors opening suddenly, vehicles cutting across, or blind junctions)?
questions.help: A junction with poor visibility is one where buildings, walls or parked vehicles hide traffic coming from the side.

options.text: Completely confident — I feel well prepared for the typical hazards
Very confident — I anticipate most hazards and respond well
Fairly confident — I manage most situations but some still worry me
Slightly confident — I am aware of the risks but often feel caught off guard
Not confident at all — I feel unprepared for these situations

questions.text: How do traffic levels and vehicle speeds on your route typically affect your journey?

options.text: Not at all — traffic does not affect my riding
Slightly — I notice traffic, but it rarely affects my comfort or route
Moderately — traffic sometimes reduces my comfort or enjoyment while cycling
Significantly — traffic often makes me feel stressed or unsafe
Very significantly — I change my route or travel time specifically to avoid heavy or fast traffic

questions.text: Which categories of road users most negatively affect your sense of safety while riding?

options.text: Car drivers
Motorcyclists or riders of scooters and mopeds
Bus drivers
Delivery vehicles (vans, cargo bikes, mopeds)
Taxi drivers or drivers of hire cars with a driver (NCC, app-based services)
Other cyclists or e-scooter riders
Pedestrians
None — no category negatively affects my feeling of safety

sections.title: Routes and road conditions
sections.description: Questions about lanes, surfaces, slopes, obstacles and signs on your route.

questions.text: How adequate is the cycling infrastructure (cycle lanes, paths, and signage) on your typical route?

options.text: Very adequate — cycling infrastructure is excellent throughout my route
Mostly adequate — infrastructure is reasonably good along most of my route
Partially adequate — infrastructure covers part of my route
Inadequate — some provision exists but it is fragmented or poorly designed
Very inadequate — little or no cycling infrastructure exists

questions.text: Which of the following physical barriers do you face on your bicycle or e-scooter route? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Uneven or poorly maintained road surfaces (potholes, patches, cobblestones)
Steep or sudden changes in gradient
Parked cars or vehicles blocking cycle lanes
Pedestrians walking in cycle lanes
Road furniture blocking cycle paths (bins, signage, advertising boards)
Lack of cycle-friendly crossings or traffic signals
Poorly designed junctions or roundabouts
Tram tracks
Edges of the sharing area, so I cannot leave the vehicle where I arrive
Stairs or steps on the route with no ramp or wheel channel
I don't face any physical barrier

questions.text: If you encounter poor road or path surfaces (potholes, cobblestones, or uneven ground), how does it affect your riding?

options.text: It does not affect my riding at all
I notice it but continue without changing my behaviour
I slow down or adjust my line but stay on the same route
I actively avoid roads with poor surfaces, even if the alternative is longer
Poor surfaces significantly limit where and how often I can ride

questions.text: To what extent does the steepness of your route affect your riding?

options.text: Not at all
Slightly — I notice hills but they do not significantly affect my journey
Moderately — hills slow me down or increase my effort noticeably
Significantly — I avoid steep routes when possible
Extremely — hills are a major barrier that limits where I can ride

questions.text: How does the quality of signs and wayfinding on your route affect your journey?
questions.help: Wayfinding means the signs, maps and arrows that show the way to a place.

options.text: Not at all — I can navigate easily regardless of signage quality
Slightly — signs are occasionally helpful
Moderately — I rely on signs to confirm my route
Significantly — unclear or missing signs sometimes disrupt my journey
Very significantly — poor signage makes navigation difficult without GPS or phone apps

sections.title: Lighting, parking and improvements
sections.description: Questions about riding after dark, parking and what would help you ride more.

questions.text: How does street lighting affect your decision to ride after dark, both for seeing the road and for feeling safe from other people?

options.text: Lighting levels have no influence on my decision to ride after dark
I notice poor lighting but it does not change when or where I ride
In poorly lit areas I ride more slowly or more carefully
I take significantly longer routes to stay in well-lit areas
I do not ride after dark because of poor lighting
I do not ride after dark for other reasons

questions.text: How would you describe the availability of parking for your bicycle or e-scooter at your most frequent destination?

options.text: Very adequate — secure and convenient parking is always available
Mostly adequate — I can usually find a suitable place to park
Partially adequate — parking is available but not always convenient or secure
Inadequate — parking exists but is too limited or too far from my destination
Very inadequate — there is nowhere secure to park my bicycle or e-scooter
I only use shared vehicles, so I don't need parking

questions.text: Has the lack of secure parking ever caused you to change your plans or leave your bicycle or e-scooter at home?

options.text: Never
Rarely
Sometimes
Often
Always
I only use shared vehicles, so I don't need parking

questions.text: What improvements would most encourage you to ride a bicycle or e-scooter more often or for longer distances?
questions.help: A physically separated cycle lane is divided from motor traffic by a kerb, posts or a barrier, not only by a painted line.

options.text: More dedicated and physically separated cycle lanes
Better road surface quality on cycling routes
More secure parking for bicycles and e-scooters, at destinations and near home
Reduced vehicle speeds in residential areas
Better cycle-friendly junctions and crossings
More trees and shade along cycling routes
Better street lighting on cycling routes
Safe riding courses for bicycles or e-scooters
Financial incentives (e.g., employer cycling allowance, subsidised bike purchase)
A larger sharing service with more bicycles, e-scooters or stations
Continuous cycle routes connecting neighbourhoods
Being able to take a bicycle or e-scooter on buses, trams, the metro or trains
Nothing — I am satisfied with current conditions

این پرسشنامه SmartUrbanity درباره تجربه شما هنگام استفاده از دوچرخه یا دوچرخه برقی است. پاسخ‌های شما کمک می‌کند شرایط و موانعی را که مردم هنگام دوچرخه‌سواری در شهر با آن روبه‌رو می‌شوند بهتر بشناسیم و راه‌هایی برای ایمن‌تر، دسترس‌پذیرتر و کاربردی‌تر شدن دوچرخه‌سواری روزانه پیدا کنیم. شرکت در این پرسشنامه داوطلبانه است. پاسخ‌های شما به نام شما مرتبط نمی‌شود: پاسخ‌ها با یک کد مستعار که از نشانی ایمیل شما ساخته می‌شود ذخیره می‌شوند تا پاسخ‌های شما به پرسشنامه‌های مختلف SmartUrbanity بتوانند با هم تحلیل شوند.

This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience as a cyclist or e-bike rider. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when cycling in the city, and identify opportunities to make cycling safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience as a cyclist or e-bike rider. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when cycling in the city, and identify opportunities to make cycling safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

Questo questionario SmartUrbanity si concentra sulla tua esperienza come ciclista o utilizzatore/utilizzatrice di e-bike. Le tue risposte ci aiutano a comprendere le condizioni e gli ostacoli che le persone incontrano quando si spostano in bicicletta in città e a individuare opportunità per rendere la mobilità ciclistica più sicura, accessibile e pratica negli spostamenti quotidiani. La partecipazione è volontaria. Le tue risposte non sono collegate al tuo nome: vengono salvate con un codice pseudonimo ricavato dal tuo indirizzo email, così che le risposte ai diversi questionari SmartUrbanity possano essere analizzate insieme.

welcome_page.image_alt: #Bicycle and a route between two points
welcome_page.description:
This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience as a cyclist or e-bike rider. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when cycling in the city, and identify opportunities to make cycling safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

sections.title: Cycling Habits
sections.description: Questions about how and when you cycle as part of your daily travel.

questions.text: Do you cycle (including e-bikes) as a mode of travel at least once a week?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.text: Which type of bicycle do you most often use?

options.text: Standard pedal bicycle (private)
Electric bicycle / e-bike (private)
Shared / hire bicycle (docked or dockless)
Shared / hire e-bike
Cargo bike or adapted bike

questions.text: How confident are you cycling in urban traffic in your city?

options.text: Not confident at all — I avoid cycling in traffic
Not very confident — I cycle only when I have no alternative
Neither confident nor unconfident
Somewhat confident — I manage most situations comfortably
Very confident — I cycle in all conditions without difficulty
I have never cycled in urban traffic

questions.text: How adequate is the cycling infrastructure (cycle lanes, paths, and signage) on your typical route?

options.text: Very inadequate — little or no cycling infrastructure exists
Inadequate — some provision exists but it is fragmented or poorly designed
Partially adequate — infrastructure covers part of my route
Mostly adequate — infrastructure is reasonably good along most of my route
Very adequate — cycling infrastructure is excellent throughout my route

questions.text: Which of the following physical barriers do you face on your cycling route? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Uneven or poorly maintained road surfaces (potholes, patches, cobblestones)
Steep or sudden changes in gradient
Parked cars or vehicles blocking cycle lanes
Pedestrians or e-scooters using cycle lanes
Road furniture blocking cycle paths (bins, signage, advertising boards)
Lack of cycle-friendly crossings or traffic signals
Poorly designed junctions or roundabouts
I don't face any physical barrier

questions.text: If you encounter poor road or path surfaces (potholes, cobblestones, or uneven ground), how does it affect your cycling?

options.text: It does not affect my cycling at all
I notice it but continue without changing my behaviour
I slow down or adjust my line but stay on the same route
I actively avoid roads with poor surfaces, even if the alternative is longer
Poor surfaces significantly limit where and how often I can cycle

questions.text: To what extent does the steepness of your route affect your cycling?

options.text: Not at all
Slightly — I notice hills but they do not significantly affect my journey
Moderately — hills slow me down or increase my effort noticeably
Significantly — I avoid steep routes when possible
Extremely — hills are a major barrier that limits where I can cycle

questions.text: How does the quality of signs and wayfinding on your cycling route affect your journey?

options.text: Not at all — I can navigate easily regardless of signage quality
Slightly — signs are occasionally helpful
Moderately — I rely on signs to confirm my route
Significantly — unclear or missing signs sometimes disrupt my journey
Very significantly — poor signage makes navigation difficult without GPS or phone apps

questions.text: How do traffic levels and vehicle speeds on your cycling route typically affect your journey?

options.text: Not at all — traffic does not affect my cycling experience
Slightly — I notice traffic, but it rarely affects my comfort or route
Moderately — traffic sometimes reduces my comfort or enjoyment while cycling
Significantly — traffic often makes me feel stressed or unsafe
Very significantly — I change my route or travel time specifically to avoid heavy or fast traffic

questions.text: Which categories of road users most negatively affect your sense of safety while cycling?

options.text: Car drivers
Motorcycle or scooter riders
Bus drivers
Delivery vehicles (vans, cargo bikes, scooters)
Taxi or ride-hailing drivers
Other cyclists
E-scooter riders
Pedestrians
None — no category negatively affects my feeling of safety

questions.text: How confident are you in your ability to anticipate and react to dangerous situations while cycling (e.g., car doors opening suddenly, vehicles cutting across, or blind junctions)?

options.text: Not confident at all — I feel unprepared for these situations
Slightly confident — I am aware of the risks but often feel caught off guard
Moderately confident — I manage most situations but some still worry me
Quite confident — I anticipate most hazards and respond well
Very confident — I feel well prepared for all typical cycling hazards

questions.text: How does street lighting affect your decision to cycle after dark?

options.text: Lighting levels have no influence on my decision to cycle after dark
I notice poor lighting but it does not change when or where I cycle
I cycle at reduced speed or stay on higher-lit roads in poorly lit areas
I take significantly longer routes to stay in well-lit areas
I do not cycle after dark because of poor lighting

questions.text: How would you describe the availability of bicycle parking at your most frequent destination?

options.text: Very inadequate — there is nowhere secure to park my bicycle
Inadequate — parking exists but is too limited or too far from my destination
Partially adequate — parking is available but not always convenient or secure
Mostly adequate — I can usually find a suitable place to park
Very adequate — secure and convenient parking is always available

questions.text: Has the lack of secure bicycle parking ever caused you to change your travel plans or leave your bike at home?

options.text: Never
Rarely
Sometimes
Often
Always — lack of parking is a constant barrier to cycling

questions.text: What improvements would most encourage you to cycle more often or for longer distances?

options.text: More dedicated and physically separated cycle lanes
Better road surface quality on cycling routes
More secure bicycle parking at destinations
More secure bicycle storage near home
Reduced vehicle speeds in residential areas
Better cycle-friendly junctions and crossings
More trees and shade along cycling routes
Better street lighting on cycling routes
Access to cycle training or skills courses
Financial incentives (e.g., employer cycling allowance, subsidised bike purchase)
Nothing — I am satisfied with current conditions

de.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Dieser SmartUrbanity-Fragebogen befasst sich mit Ihrer Erfahrung beim Radfahren oder mit dem E-Bike. Ihre Antworten helfen uns zu verstehen, welche Bedingungen und Hindernisse Menschen beim Radfahren in der Stadt erleben und wie Radfahren sicherer, zugänglicher und alltagstauglicher werden kann. Die Teilnahme ist freiwillig. Ihre Antworten werden nicht mit Ihrem Namen verknüpft: Sie werden unter einem pseudonymen Code gespeichert, der aus Ihrer E-Mail-Adresse abgeleitet wird, damit Ihre Antworten auf die verschiedenen SmartUrbanity-Fragebögen gemeinsam ausgewertet werden können.

tr.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Bu SmartUrbanity anketi bisiklet veya elektrikli bisiklet kullanma deneyiminizle ilgilidir. Yanıtlarınız, insanların şehirde bisiklet kullanırken karşılaştığı koşulları ve engelleri anlamamıza ve bisikleti günlük yaşamda daha güvenli, erişilebilir ve kullanışlı hale getirecek fırsatları belirlememize yardımcı olur. Katılım gönüllüdür. Yanıtlarınız adınızla ilişkilendirilmez: farklı SmartUrbanity anketlerine verdiğiniz yanıtların birlikte analiz edilebilmesi için e-posta adresinizden türetilen takma adlı bir kodla saklanır.

Ez a SmartUrbanity kérdőív a kerékpárral vagy elektromos kerékpárral szerzett tapasztalatairól szól. Válaszai segítenek megérteni, milyen körülményekkel és akadályokkal találkoznak az emberek városi kerékpározás közben, és hogyan lehet a kerékpározást biztonságosabbá, hozzáférhetőbbé és a mindennapokban könnyebben használhatóvá tenni. This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience riding a bicycle, e-bike or e-scooter. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when riding a bicycle or e-scooter in the city, and identify opportunities to make these trips safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience riding a bicycle, e-bike or e-scooter. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when riding a bicycle or e-scooter in the city, and identify opportunities to make these trips safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

":"

Ce questionnaire SmartUrbanity porte sur votre expérience à vélo, à vélo électrique ou en trottinette électrique. Vos réponses nous aident à comprendre les conditions et les obstacles rencontrés en ville et à trouver des moyens de rendre ces déplacements plus sûrs, plus accessibles et plus pratiques au quotidien. La participation est volontaire. Vos réponses ne sont pas associées à votre nom : elles sont enregistrées sous un code pseudonyme dérivé de votre adresse e-mail, afin que vos réponses aux différents questionnaires SmartUrbanity puissent être analysées ensemble.

This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience riding a bicycle, e-bike or e-scooter. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when riding a bicycle or e-scooter in the city, and identify opportunities to make these trips safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

welcome_page.title: Welcome to Your Experience With Cycling and E-scooters
welcome_page.image_alt: #Bicycle and a route between two points
welcome_page.description:
This SmartUrbanity questionnaire focuses on your experience riding a bicycle, e-bike or e-scooter. Your answers help us understand the conditions and barriers people face when riding a bicycle or e-scooter in the city, and identify opportunities to make these trips safer, more accessible, and more practical for everyday travel. Participation is voluntary. Your answers are not linked to your name. They are stored under a pseudonymous code derived from your email address, so that your answers to different SmartUrbanity questionnaires can be analysed together.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

final_page.title: Thank you!
final_page.description: Your submission has been recorded. Thank you for taking the time to complete the questionnaire.

questionnaire.title: 8. Your Experience With Cycling and E-scooters

sections.title: Bicycle or e-scooter use and traffic
sections.description: Questions about whether you ride a bicycle or e-scooter and how you feel in traffic.

questions.text: Do you ride a bicycle (including e-bikes) or an e-scooter, your own or a shared one, at least once a week to get to places?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.text: What keeps you from riding a bicycle or e-scooter, or from riding more often? (Select all that apply)
questions.help: We ask this to understand what limits cycling and e-scooter use for different people. Answering is optional, and you can also choose not to say.

options.text: I don't need to: other ways of getting around suit me better
Hills and steep slopes
Traffic feels too dangerous
No cycle lanes or no continuous routes to where I go
Nowhere secure to keep it at home or to park it at my destination
I don't have a bicycle or e-scooter, and there is no sharing service near me
It costs too much (the vehicle or the sharing service)
I don't know how to ride a bicycle or e-scooter, or I don't feel up to it
My health, a disability or my age makes it difficult
Destinations are too far away
Heat or bad weather
I carry heavy things or accompany children or other people

questions.text: Which type of bicycle or e-scooter do you use most often?
questions.help: A cargo bike has a large box or platform for carrying children or goods. Shared bikes with a station are picked up and returned at fixed points; those without a station can be left anywhere within the service area.

options.text: Standard pedal bicycle (private)
Electric bicycle / e-bike (private)
Shared / hire bicycle (docked or dockless)
Shared / hire e-bike
Cargo bike or adapted bike
E-scooter (private)
Shared / hire e-scooter

questions.text: How comfortable do you feel riding your bicycle or e-scooter in urban traffic in your city?

options.text: Very comfortable — I ride in all conditions without difficulty
Fairly comfortable — I manage most situations
Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable
Not very comfortable — I ride in traffic only when I have no alternative
Not at all comfortable
I don't ride in urban traffic

questions.text: How confident are you in your ability to anticipate and react to dangerous situations while riding (e.g., car doors opening suddenly, vehicles cutting across, or blind junctions)?
questions.help: A junction with poor visibility is one where buildings, walls or parked vehicles hide traffic coming from the side.

options.text: Completely confident — I feel well prepared for the typical hazards
Very confident — I anticipate most hazards and respond well
Fairly confident — I manage most situations but some still worry me
Slightly confident — I am aware of the risks but often feel caught off guard
Not confident at all — I feel unprepared for these situations

questions.text: How do traffic levels and vehicle speeds on your route typically affect your journey?

options.text: Not at all — traffic does not affect my riding
Slightly — I notice traffic, but it rarely affects my comfort or route
Moderately — traffic sometimes reduces my comfort or enjoyment while cycling
Significantly — traffic often makes me feel stressed or unsafe
Very significantly — I change my route or travel time specifically to avoid heavy or fast traffic

questions.text: Which categories of road users most negatively affect your sense of safety while riding?

options.text: Car drivers
Motorcyclists or riders of scooters and mopeds
Bus drivers
Delivery vehicles (vans, cargo bikes, mopeds)
Taxi drivers or drivers of hire cars with a driver (NCC, app-based services)
Other cyclists or e-scooter riders
Pedestrians
None — no category negatively affects my feeling of safety

sections.title: Routes and road conditions
sections.description: Questions about lanes, surfaces, slopes, obstacles and signs on your route.

questions.text: How adequate is the cycling infrastructure (cycle lanes, paths, and signage) on your typical route?

options.text: Very adequate — cycling infrastructure is excellent throughout my route
Mostly adequate — infrastructure is reasonably good along most of my route
Partially adequate — infrastructure covers part of my route
Inadequate — some provision exists but it is fragmented or poorly designed
Very inadequate — little or no cycling infrastructure exists

questions.text: Which of the following physical barriers do you face on your bicycle or e-scooter route? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Uneven or poorly maintained road surfaces (potholes, patches, cobblestones)
Steep or sudden changes in gradient
Parked cars or vehicles blocking cycle lanes
Pedestrians walking in cycle lanes
Road furniture blocking cycle paths (bins, signage, advertising boards)
Lack of cycle-friendly crossings or traffic signals
Poorly designed junctions or roundabouts
Tram tracks
Edges of the sharing area, so I cannot leave the vehicle where I arrive
Stairs or steps on the route with no ramp or wheel channel
I don't face any physical barrier

questions.text: If you encounter poor road or path surfaces (potholes, cobblestones, or uneven ground), how does it affect your riding?

options.text: It does not affect my riding at all
I notice it but continue without changing my behaviour
I slow down or adjust my line but stay on the same route
I actively avoid roads with poor surfaces, even if the alternative is longer
Poor surfaces significantly limit where and how often I can ride

questions.text: To what extent does the steepness of your route affect your riding?

options.text: Not at all
Slightly — I notice hills but they do not significantly affect my journey
Moderately — hills slow me down or increase my effort noticeably
Significantly — I avoid steep routes when possible
Extremely — hills are a major barrier that limits where I can ride

questions.text: How does the quality of signs and wayfinding on your route affect your journey?
questions.help: Wayfinding means the signs, maps and arrows that show the way to a place.

options.text: Not at all — I can navigate easily regardless of signage quality
Slightly — signs are occasionally helpful
Moderately — I rely on signs to confirm my route
Significantly — unclear or missing signs sometimes disrupt my journey
Very significantly — poor signage makes navigation difficult without GPS or phone apps

sections.title: Lighting, parking and improvements
sections.description: Questions about riding after dark, parking and what would help you ride more.

questions.text: How does street lighting affect your decision to ride after dark, both for seeing the road and for feeling safe from other people?

options.text: Lighting levels have no influence on my decision to ride after dark
I notice poor lighting but it does not change when or where I ride
In poorly lit areas I ride more slowly or more carefully
I take significantly longer routes to stay in well-lit areas
I do not ride after dark because of poor lighting
I do not ride after dark for other reasons

questions.text: How would you describe the availability of parking for your bicycle or e-scooter at your most frequent destination?

options.text: Very adequate — secure and convenient parking is always available
Mostly adequate — I can usually find a suitable place to park
Partially adequate — parking is available but not always convenient or secure
Inadequate — parking exists but is too limited or too far from my destination
Very inadequate — there is nowhere secure to park my bicycle or e-scooter
I only use shared vehicles, so I don't need parking

questions.text: Has the lack of secure parking ever caused you to change your plans or leave your bicycle or e-scooter at home?

options.text: Never
Rarely
Sometimes
Often
Always
I only use shared vehicles, so I don't need parking

questions.text: What improvements would most encourage you to ride a bicycle or e-scooter more often or for longer distances?
questions.help: A physically separated cycle lane is divided from motor traffic by a kerb, posts or a barrier, not only by a painted line.

options.text: More dedicated and physically separated cycle lanes
Better road surface quality on cycling routes
More secure parking for bicycles and e-scooters, at destinations and near home
Reduced vehicle speeds in residential areas
Better cycle-friendly junctions and crossings
More trees and shade along cycling routes
Better street lighting on cycling routes
Safe riding courses for bicycles or e-scooters
Financial incentives (e.g., employer cycling allowance, subsidised bike purchase)
A larger sharing service with more bicycles, e-scooters or stations
Continuous cycle routes connecting neighbourhoods
Being able to take a bicycle or e-scooter on buses, trams, the metro or trains
Nothing — I am satisfied with current conditions

it.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Questo questionario SmartUrbanity si concentra sulla tua esperienza in bicicletta, bicicletta elettrica o monopattino. Le tue risposte ci aiutano a comprendere le condizioni e gli ostacoli che le persone incontrano quando si spostano in bicicletta o in monopattino in città e a individuare opportunità per rendere questi spostamenti più sicuri, accessibili e pratici nella vita quotidiana. La partecipazione è volontaria. Le tue risposte non sono collegate al tuo nome: vengono salvate con un codice pseudonimo ricavato dal tuo indirizzo email, così che le risposte ai diversi questionari SmartUrbanity possano essere analizzate insieme.

fr.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Ce questionnaire SmartUrbanity porte sur votre expérience à vélo, à vélo électrique ou en trottinette électrique. Vos réponses nous aident à comprendre les conditions et les obstacles rencontrés en ville et à trouver des moyens de rendre ces déplacements plus sûrs, plus accessibles et plus pratiques au quotidien. La participation est volontaire. Vos réponses ne sont pas associées à votre nom : elles sont enregistrées sous un code pseudonyme dérivé de votre adresse e-mail, afin que vos réponses aux différents questionnaires SmartUrbanity puissent être analysées ensemble.

de.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Dieser SmartUrbanity-Fragebogen befasst sich mit Ihrer Erfahrung mit Fahrrad, E-Bike oder E-Scooter. Ihre Antworten helfen uns zu verstehen, welche Bedingungen und Hindernisse Menschen mit dem Fahrrad oder E-Scooter in der Stadt erleben und wie diese Fahrten sicherer, zugänglicher und alltagstauglicher werden können. Die Teilnahme ist freiwillig. Ihre Antworten werden nicht mit Ihrem Namen verknüpft: Sie werden unter einem pseudonymen Code gespeichert, der aus Ihrer E-Mail-Adresse abgeleitet wird, damit Ihre Antworten auf die verschiedenen SmartUrbanity-Fragebögen gemeinsam ausgewertet werden können.

hu.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Ez a SmartUrbanity kérdőív a kerékpárral, elektromos kerékpárral vagy elektromos rollerrel szerzett tapasztalatairól szól. Válaszai segítenek megérteni, milyen körülményekkel és akadályokkal találkoznak az emberek, amikor kerékpárral vagy rollerrel közlekednek a városban, és hogyan lehet ezeket az utakat biztonságosabbá, hozzáférhetőbbé és a mindennapokban könnyebben használhatóvá tenni. A részvétel önkéntes. Válaszai nem kapcsolódnak a nevéhez: egy, az e-mail-címéből képzett álnevesített kóddal tároljuk őket, hogy a különböző SmartUrbanity-kérdőívekre adott válaszait együtt lehessen elemezni.

it.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Questo questionario SmartUrbanity si concentra sulla tua esperienza in bicicletta, bicicletta elettrica o monopattino. Le tue risposte ci aiutano a comprendere le condizioni e gli ostacoli che le persone incontrano quando si spostano in bicicletta o in monopattino in città e a individuare opportunità per rendere questi spostamenti più sicuri, accessibili e pratici nella vita quotidiana. La partecipazione è volontaria. Le tue risposte non sono collegate al tuo nome: vengono salvate con un codice pseudonimo ricavato dal tuo indirizzo email, così che le risposte ai diversi questionari SmartUrbanity possano essere analizzate insieme.

fr.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Ce questionnaire SmartUrbanity porte sur votre expérience à vélo, à vélo électrique ou en trottinette électrique. Vos réponses nous aident à comprendre les conditions et les obstacles rencontrés en ville et à trouver des moyens de rendre ces déplacements plus sûrs, plus accessibles et plus pratiques au quotidien. tr.#<p>This SmartUrbanity questionnaire foc:
Bu SmartUrbanity anketi bisiklet, elektrikli bisiklet veya elektrikli scooter kullanma deneyiminizle ilgilidir. Yanıtlarınız, insanların şehirde bisiklet veya elektrikli scooter kullanırken karşılaştığı koşulları ve engelleri anlamamıza ve bu yolculukları günlük yaşamda daha güvenli, erişilebilir ve kullanışlı hale getirecek fırsatları belirlememize yardımcı olur. Katılım gönüllüdür. Yanıtlarınız adınızla ilişkilendirilmez: farklı SmartUrbanity anketlerine verdiğiniz yanıtların birlikte analiz edilebilmesi için e-posta adresinizden türetilen takma adlı bir kodla saklanır.

Ez a SmartUrbanity kérdőív a kerékpárral, elektromos kerékpárral vagy elektromos rollerrel szerzett tapasztalatairól szól. Válaszai segítenek megérteni, milyen körülményekkel és akadályokkal találkoznak az emberek, amikor kerékpárral vagy rollerrel közlekednek a városban, és hogyan lehet ezeket az utakat biztonságosabbá, hozzáférhetőbbé és a mindennapokban könnyebben használhatóvá tenni. A részvétel önkéntes. Válaszai nem kapcsolódnak a nevéhez: egy, az e-mail-címéből képzett álnevesített kóddal tároljuk őket, hogy a különböző SmartUrbanity-kérdőívekre adott válaszait együtt lehessen elemezni.
